subject: pe
title: Applications: Analysing Sport
welcome_lead: Apply movement analysis to real sporting actions — from kicks to throws.
meta_desc: GCSE PE Movement Analysis applications: identifying levers, planes and axes in sport.
final_note: Superb! You can now decode the mechanics of any sporting action.

concepts.def: Vertical axis from head to toe, used in spinning.
Effort arm longer than load arm — easier lifting.
Load arm longer than effort arm — needs more force.
Movement of a limb away from the body's midline.

walkthroughs.body_html: Each plane has a partner axis: sagittal plane + transverse axis (somersault), frontal plane + frontal axis (cartwheel), transverse plane + longitudinal axis (discus spin, ice-skater pirouette).
A football kick is a 3rd class lever at the knee (effort from quadriceps between knee joint fulcrum and foot load). It happens in the sagittal plane around the transverse axis, using knee extension.

A calf raise is a 2nd class lever. The effort arm (from ball of foot to ankle muscle) is longer than the load arm, giving mechanical advantage — small force lifts big weight, but the range and speed are limited.

mcqs.q: A cartwheel takes place in which plane and axis?
Which lever class typically gives mechanical advantage?

numericals.q: If effort arm is 60 cm and load arm is 20 cm, what is the mechanical advantage?
